activation.note: Activation retains alternative A11Y-URN and filename-token identification, the browser-spec definition, and generated/vendor exclusions. Filename boundary interpretation and examples are declared additions consistent with token-based identification. Parser, configuration, and detector-dependent facts honestly require new observers; path and edit-operation facts are directly observable.

audit.summary: All 21 segments survive at their claimed destinations, with mandatory harness execution, fail-capable violations assertions, accepted matchers, alias support, and the tautology prohibition retained. The rewrite adds no undeclared coder obligation or waiver, and uses no shared nodes; its then describes one cohesive accessibility-harness obligation.

segmentChecks.note: The alternative A11Y identification signals, required package import with aliasing, analyze call, and all accepted fail-capable matcher forms survive across given/then/prefer/evidence and verifier_detail.
avoid[2] and verifier_detail[3] retain both the toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0) example and the general rule that tautologies do not count as assertions.
The browser-spec definition retains the Playwright *.e2e.ts branch, every listed header journey-marker form, and coverage of misnamed files.
Both activation and verifier_detail expressly exclude a unit test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string.
The rationale and the two failure modes—never running axe and never asserting on its result—are retained in why and avoid.
prefer[2] reproduces the canonical AxeBuilder construction, awaited analyze call, and empty-violations assertion.
All four vendored/generated tree names and the never-scan rule remain in verifier_detail and activation doesNotFire.
The validator type and htmx_e2e_detector reference remain in audit, with the corresponding no-finding check in evidence.

risks: The coder-facing fields do not define an a11y filename token or restrict matching to the basename, so a weak tester could mishandle longer-word substrings or an a11y directory name.
They omit the browser_spec definition and string-literal exclusion, which could lead a weak tester to add axe to an inapplicable unit test or mishandle a misnamed browser spec.
They do not mention the node_modules, dist, build, and _generated scanning exclusions; those details require reading activation or verifier_detail rather than only the coder-facing fields.

unobservable: file_kind=a11y_test_urn requires a new test-URN parser/observer.
file_kind=browser_spec requires a new header-comment parser and Playwright-configuration observer.
finding=htmx_e2e_detector:a11y-harness requires the detector or a new observer for its findings.

review.summary: The knowledge-rich segments checked are preserved, with no dropped/shared segments or auditor non-PRESERVED findings to re-judge, so I agree with PASS. The happy-path implementation is clear, but the coder-facing fields alone leave applicability ambiguities around filename tokens, browser-spec scope, and excluded trees. Activation is deterministic once the explicitly declared parser, configuration, and detector observers supply their facts.
